calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(2), an ancillary building may be used for living accommodation in one garden suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Overrides the 10.5.60.1(2) prohibition on living accommodation in ancillary buildings, for one garden suite. No zone is named.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(3), an ancillary building may have both food preparation facilities and sanitary facilities in a garden suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: Overrides the 'not both' limb of 10.5.60.1(3) for a garden suite. Interior fit-out is a design fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A garden suite may have both a kitchen and washroom facilities. We do not check interior fit-out.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 10.5.60.1(4), above-ground parts of an ancillary building containing a garden suite may be erected before the main walls and roof of the residential building on the same lot are erected and completed.
calculation_handling.gaps: Overrides the construction-timing prohibition of 10.5.60.1(4) for an ancillary building containing a garden suite; a sequencing rule, not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A garden suite building may be built before the main house on the lot is finished. This is a construction-timing rule we do not evaluate.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.5.60.1(1), a home occupation is permitted in a garden suite that is exclusively and separately occupied as a principal residence, applying Section 150.5 as if the garden suite were a dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Home occupation is not a vocab.uses token; the dwelling_unit token records the 'as if it is a dwelling unit' treatment. Occupancy (principal residence) is not a lot fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A home business may operate in a garden suite that is someone's principal residence, under the home occupation rules in Section 150.5. We do not evaluate home occupations.

calculation_handling.description: Despite 150.13.20.1(1), a short-term rental is permitted in an ancillary building if it is in a garden suite that is exclusively and separately occupied as a principal residence.
calculation_handling.gaps: Short-term rental is not a vocab.uses token. Occupancy (principal residence) is not a lot fact; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: A short-term rental is allowed in a garden suite that is someone's principal residence. We do not evaluate short-term rental use.

calculation_handling.description: A maximum of one ancillary building containing either a garden suite or a laneway suite is permitted on a lot, and a lot may not contain both a garden suite and a laneway suite.
calculation_handling.gaps: The limit is written 'a maximum of one'; keyed as the numeral 1 units. The second sentence (a lot may not contain both a garden suite and a laneway suite) is a prohibition carried by this same unit; it is described here rather than split into a separate unit.

150.7.20.1(1).explanation: These rules let a garden suite do things an ordinary accessory building cannot: be lived in (one garden suite), have both a kitchen and washroom, be built before the main house is finished, host a home business, and be used as a short-term rental if it is someone's principal residence.

150.7.20.1(2).explanation: A lot can have only one accessory building containing a garden suite or a laneway suite, and cannot have both a garden suite and a laneway suite.
